factual_methodological.summary: Central September 23 market and macro observations were checked against primary U.S. Treasury and S&P Global evidence and suitable event reporting. The Treasury curve values, U.S. and euro-area PMI deltas and UK PMI direction are supported. Observed facts are separated from inference and conditional transmission.

novelty_repetition.summary: Compared with MT-GM-2026-09-21, MT-GM-2026-09-22 and MT-GM-2026-09-23. The September 23 U.S. PMI acceleration and 15 bp one-session rise in the 10-year Treasury to 5.11% provide a material new delta. Oil/Gulf risk is demoted to background rather than repeated as the dominant thesis.

editorial_publication_readiness.opening: Direct thesis-led opening; no generic assessment or summary heading and no form-like field sequence.
editorial_publication_readiness.headings: Analytical headings identify the object and mechanism rather than functioning as empty category labels.
editorial_publication_readiness.language_localization: English reads as native institutional research prose and PT-BR is natural and semantically equivalent; retained market terms are conventional or contextually explained.
editorial_publication_readiness.repetition: The central growth-driven rate mechanism is developed rather than mechanically restated; the prior oil thesis is explicitly subordinated to the new delta.
editorial_publication_readiness.cohesion: Progression runs from thesis and rate repricing through cross-asset transmission, regional policy differences, emerging-market transmission, residual oil risk and second-order effects.
editorial_publication_readiness.template_meta_qa: No prompt, QA history, internal classification fields or retrabalho scars are exposed to the reader.

contextual_depth.summary: The report incorporates the material institutional and geopolitical context needed for the current mechanism: central-bank constraints, Gulf physical-risk transmission and differing U.S./euro-area/UK/China monetary conditions. No ornamental historical section is required for this daily brief.

conflict_security_social_change.summary: Gulf conflict is treated as a conditional transmission risk through physical throughput, freight, insurance and energy prices rather than as an unsupported operational claim. Geopolitical uncertainty is separated from observed market and macro data.

visual_evidence_readiness.signature: brief: 1 explicit line chart + 1 Markdown evidence table + 1 causal flow + 1 regional transmission map (4 useful visuals total)
visual_evidence_readiness.summary: The chart uses a single percentage unit across Treasury maturities and dates; the table exposes directly comparable observations; flow arrows reproduce mechanisms defended in prose; the map represents regional transmission rather than false geographic precision. EN/PT-BR values, units and mechanisms are semantically equivalent.
visual_evidence_readiness.limitations: The Treasury chart compares maturities rather than a single homogeneous time series, but all observations use the same yield unit and are explicitly labeled by maturity and date.

contrary_evidence: Stronger activity can support earnings sufficiently for equities to coexist with high sovereign yields, so higher yields do not mechanically imply weaker equities.
Further energy-price declines combined with cooling U.S. activity and inflation would weaken the growth-driven rate-shock thesis.
China's liquidity operation is short-term holiday liquidity management and does not establish a structural stimulus shift.
limitations: Flash PMI readings are survey-based preliminary indicators rather than final national-accounts data.
Market observations are a September 23 U.S.-close snapshot and do not establish durable capital-flow reallocations without subsequent flow evidence.
Gulf conflict transmission remains contingent on realized export throughput, freight, insurance and refined-product availability.
notes: Approved as a new daily Global Macro brief. The new dominant mechanism is a verified growth-driven repricing of long U.S. rates, materially distinct from the oil-relief thesis that dominated the preceding editions.

en.title: Global Macro — Growth, not oil, pushes the rate shock into a new phase
en.deck: A sharp U.S. growth surprise pushed the 10-year Treasury above 5.1%, turning resilient activity itself into the new source of tighter global financial conditions while Europe also accelerated.
en.regime: Growth-driven rate tightening layered on top of unresolved energy and geopolitical risk
en.key_risk: Resilient U.S. and euro-area activity may keep real and nominal long yields high enough for refinancing and investment constraints to spread into credit and earnings even if oil eases.
watch: Gulf realized export and refined-product flows

pt-BR.title: Global Macro — Crescimento, e não petróleo, leva o choque de juros a uma nova fase
pt-BR.deck: Uma forte surpresa de crescimento nos EUA levou o Treasury de 10 anos acima de 5,1%, transformando a própria resistência da atividade na nova fonte de aperto das condições financeiras globais enquanto a Europa também acelerou.
pt-BR.regime: Aperto de juros movido pelo crescimento somado a risco energético e geopolítico ainda não resolvido
pt-BR.key_risk: Atividade resistente nos EUA e na zona do euro pode manter juros reais e nominais longos altos o suficiente para que restrições de refinanciamento e investimento se espalhem para crédito e lucros mesmo com alívio do petróleo.

novelty_gate.material_delta: September 23 U.S. PMI accelerated to 58.4 and the 10-year Treasury par yield rose 15 bp to 5.11%, while euro-area PMI accelerated to 53.1. This shifts the dominant mechanism from oil-relief versus high rates to growth itself sustaining tighter global rates.
novelty_gate.repeated_theme_treatment: Oil/Gulf risk is retained as background and transmission risk rather than the dominant thesis.
